messages:
incident-bot: [ALERT] service:redwood-api p95 latency breached 1200ms for 3m (hosted-us-west2). Paging on-call.
Maya (oncall): I'm on it, joining. Can someone confirm customer-facing impact?
Luke (CS): Seeing a few customer reports of slow responses in analytics dashboards, some timeouts. No-wide outage.
Maya (oncall): thanks. Starting triage — collecting top-level metrics. Ryan, can you lift traces for the past 10m?
Ryan (eng-runtime): grabbing traces now. p50 looks fine, p95 jumped from ~180ms to ~950ms starting ~2245556600. Span breakdown shows large increases in kernel_io and scheduling waits.
Ian (infra): Not seeing noisy host CPU saturations. GPU and application CPU look normal. Network egress is steady.
June (SRE): Any deploys around that time? Canary rollouts?
Ryan (eng-runtime): No deploys. Autoscaler didn't change either. No model swaps.
Maya (oncall): will reroute ~10% of traffic to the fallback model variant to reduce tail. Doing a temporary route override now.
Maya (oncall): routing change applied — traffic shift started at 2245556860. Monitoring p95.
incident-bot: [ACTION] Route override by Maya (oncall) to fallback-1 applied.
Maya (oncall): p95 dropped to ~420ms after partial shift. Good signal that heavier model variant may be amplifying tail.
Ryan (eng-runtime): attaching a snippet of the span flame graph (pasted for thread):
```
Flame graph excerpt (p95 request):
- request
  - parse_input 12ms
  - runtime_infer 380ms
    - attention_kern 50ms
    - kv_cache_load 230ms
    - kernel_io_wait 90ms
  - postproc 8ms
```

Ryan (eng-runtime): kernel_io_wait is the big one. Checking perf counters and LSM logs.
Ian (infra): I pulled dmesg on two affected nodes — saw a couple of "blk_update_request: I/O error, dev nvme0n1" around 2245556645 but they recovered. Could be transient NVMe hiccup.
June (SRE): If NVMe flakiness is in play, we should consider marking nodes unhealthy and draining. But need to confirm scope first. How many hosts show the kernel_io wait spike?
Ryan (eng-runtime): Traces map to ~7 hosts in us-west2. Other hosts in the pool are fine. Correlating with disk IO metrics now.
Maya (oncall): any active maintenance windows?
Ian (infra): No scheduled maintenance. I/O error messages correlate with a background snapshot job that kicked off at 2245556602 — looks like a backup of model artifacts to durable storage.
Ryan (eng-runtime): if backup is causing increased disk contention, that could explain elevated kv_cache_load times and kernel waits. Did we throttle snapshot IO?
Ian (infra): Not at the host layer, it's handled by a batch job that uses default IO priority. I'll reconfigure to use ionice and rate-limit.
Maya (oncall): while Ian changes that, let's spin up two warm standby hosts in that pool and move 30% traffic there to reduce load on unlucky hosts.
incident-bot: [ACTION] Maya (oncall) requested scale-up. Autoscaling triggered provisioning of 2 hosts at 2245556921.
Maya (oncall): Scale-up complete, shifting traffic. Observing p95 down to ~240ms across the board now.
Amy (product): quick note — a couple of enterprise customers saw retries and SLO alerts. Do we want CS to notify impacted customers that we mitigated and are investigating root cause?
Luke (CS): I'll draft a heads-up: "We've observed transient high latency affecting some analytics flows; we've applied routing mitigations and scaled capacity. We're investigating underlying storage operations."
June (SRE): Next for RCA: collect full kernel logs, perf counters (blockio, iostat), snapshot job metadata, and exact trace->host mapping. Also check whether any kernel patch landed recently.
Ryan (eng-runtime): Pulling perf counters for affected hosts now: blktrace shows elevated queue times aligning with snapshot window. No recent kernel upgrades in the last 48h.
Ian (infra): The snapshot job logs show 2245556602 start triggered by the model-registry garbage collection. Looks like a GC overlap with snapshot. I'll add IO niceness and reschedule the GC job to a different maintenance window.
Maya (oncall): good. For immediate action items: (1) Ian to set ionice + reschedule GC; (2) Ryan to attach trace-to-host mapping and flame graphs to the incident doc; (3) June to gather kernel/perf logs; (4) Luke to notify customers.
June (SRE): starting log bundle for affected hosts: /var/log/incident-bundles/2245556789.tar.gz (will upload link here when ready).
Ryan (eng-runtime): saving per-request trace ids and host mapping to the incident board. Example trace ids: trace-0a7f, trace-0a80, trace-0a92 — all map to host-az-west2-03 and host-az-west2-07.
Maya (oncall): any evidence of kernel-level scheduling bugs?
Ryan (eng-runtime): Not seeing scheduling anomalies outside of IO-induced waits. Perf counters: context-switch rate normal. disk_avg_queue > 50ms during the window.
Ian (infra): I applied ionice -c2 -n7 to GC worker and bumped its rate limit; rescheduled next run to off-peak. Change applied at 2245557050.
incident-bot: [CHANGE] GC job IO niceness updated by Ian (infra).
Maya (oncall): verifying that p95 remains stable. Current p95 ~210ms. Standby hosts remain warm.
Amy (product): plan for post-incident: RCA doc, timeline, and action owner to prevent GC overlapping peak traffic. Also consider adding IO throttling default for any background jobs.
June (SRE): I'll start a timeline in the RCA doc with attached logs and perf CSVs. Hypotheses to track: (A) background snapshot GC caused NVMe contention -> increased kernel_io_wait -> p95 spike; (B) transient NVMe firmware timeouts causing IO errors independent of GC; (C) subtle runtime interaction causing heavier KV cache reads on a subset of hosts. We'll validate in that order.
Maya (oncall): tagging follow-ups: Ian(Infra) owner for IO throttling + schedule change; Ryan(Runtime) owner for trace correlation and checks of kv_cache behavior; June(SRE) to produce RCA and postmortem.
Luke (CS): sent customer notice at 2245557160.
Maya (oncall): wrapping up on-call handoff notes — incident stabilized at 2245557065 after mitigation. Leaving notes for next on-call.
June (SRE): final notes for this thread: evidence strongly supports hypothesis A. Actionables: default ionice for GC, rate-limit snapshot copying, alerting on host disk_avg_queue > 30ms, and a runbook for fallback routing earlier. Assigning owners in the postmortem doc.
Ryan (eng-runtime): will add a config flag to runtime to detect KV cache cold spikes and auto-fallback earlier.
Maya (oncall): thanks everyone. Closing the page but keeping the thread for RCA.
incident-bot: [RESOLVED] Incident service:redwood-api latency p95 resolved by mitigations and capacity changes.
